title: Restriction and finite-stratum detection of the adic completion unit
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], put $R_n=(A/I^n)_X$ and $B_X=\varprojlim_nR_n$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $u$ be either a locally closed stratum immersion $S\to X$, restriction to a pro-etale site object $U\to X$, or a composite of these two restrictions. For each restricted scheme $Y=S$ or $U$, put $B_Y=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/I^n)_Y$. Identify coefficient sheaves by the maps induced from the quotient projections. Then $u^{-1}B_X\cong B_S$ (respectively $B_U$), module pullback is exact, and there are canonical isomorphisms
$$u^{-1}(K\otimes^L_{B_X}R_n)\cong u^{-1}K\otimes^L_{B_S}(A/I^n)_S,$$
with $S$ replaced by $U$ as necessary. They commute with quotient transitions and normalization maps. For the specified strict quotient tower, define $\eta_K:K\to R\lim_n(K\otimes^L_{B_X}R_n)$ as the derived constant/Rlim adjunction unit followed by Rlim of the normalized strict quotient augmentation [def-weil-pbc-exact-pullback-interface, def-weil-pbc-reduction-augmentation]. This is the quotient completion unit normalized by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Its inverse image identifies with $\eta_{u^{-1}K}$, including the map from $u^{-1}K$. Intrinsic derived $I$-completeness [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is preserved by these restrictions. For any finite stratification of $X$ [def-constructible-stratification] and chosen pro-etale covering of each stratum, $K$ is intrinsically complete if and only if all its restrictions to those covering members are intrinsically complete.

proof.text: For each restriction $u:Y\to X$, the canonical constant-ring maps identify $u^{-1}R_n$ with $(A/I^n)_Y$, since every $A/I^n$ is finite. Inverse image preserves limits for a locally closed immersion and for restriction to a pro-etale object, by the two limit-preservation lemmas. Limits of ring sheaves have their operations componentwise on the underlying limits, so these identifications induce a ring isomorphism $c_u:u^{-1}B_X\cong B_Y$. Its $n$-th projection is exactly the pullback of $B_X\to R_n$ followed by the constant-ring identification. Thus this is the coefficient map specified in the statement. For a composite restriction the same assertion follows by composing these isomorphisms: their composites with every quotient projection agree.

proof.text: For the actual stratumModulePull, exactness and additivity are the existing canonical module-pullback instances. To prove all-limit preservation, first establish it for set inverse image: use the immersion theorem or weakly-etale restriction theorem, and the canonical composition comparison for either mixed composite. Transfer this to abelian sheaves through the underlying-set comparison and the conservative limit-preserving forgetful functor. Transfer again to pure module inverse image through its natural underlying-abelian comparison. Finally use the scalar-extension equivalence along the canonical completed coefficient isomorphism. This proves stratumRestriction_limits without a Noetherian hypothesis on Y; its projection clause is the existing projection_comm theorem.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8 proof; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0E8K (lemma-restriction-K-flat), and sites-modules.tex Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits).

proof.text: Construct the ordinary normalized comparison before passing to the derived category. At each quotient level, let b be the published ordinary restriction/pullback comparison. Its mate under the two geometric module adjunctions is the sectionwise-identity direct-image comparison. Take its inverse mate under the two scalar-extension adjunctions. The iterated-mate/conjugation identity identifies its conjugate with that direct-image isomorphism, so the scalar mate is invertible. Compose b with scalar restriction of the inverse scalar mate. The unit-mate identity proves that this level isomorphism carries the pulled-back quotient unit to the target quotient unit. The specified units agree with the scalar adjunction units by their formulas on tensor generators. Each completed coefficient projection is sectionwise surjective; hence every ordinary quotient unit is epi, as proved in completed-constant-coefficient-equivalence. Exact module pullback preserves these epis. For the level comparisons, precompose each proposed transition or module-naturality square with this epi: the unit equations and the existing augmentation's naturality make both paths equal. Cancellation assembles the level isomorphisms into one natural strict-tower isomorphism and proves its uniqueness. Then keep the existing derived construction: resolve complexes by K-flat complexes with flat terms, use ringed-topos pullback preservation of K-flatness and the computing reduction counits, and descend the ordinary comparison uniquely along the fully faithful restriction to resolving representatives. The universal-counit equation extends to every complex by naturality and cancellation of the invertible image of a resolution. This gives exactly StratumReductionFormula. Only finite evaluation and quotient-normalization remain existing named obligations.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); normalized augmented strict-tower assertion of the cited node.

proof.text: The finite coefficient naturality square is proved using the constant-ring comparison. For finite quotient normalization, identify the source and target normalization maps as conjugates of the inverse scalar restriction compositors using lem-weil-pbc-reduction-normalization-scalar-mate. The restriction/pullback squares respect scalar composition by lem-weil-pbc-restriction-pullback-scalar-composition. Apply the horizontal mates composition law and the two conjugation/vertical-composition laws to obtain the inverse finite-pullback square, then cancel its three invertible finite comparisons. This proves stratumReduction_normalization. Finite evaluation remains its existing named obligation. For strict augmentation compatibility, first prove the general exact-square localization-factor equation from mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac. On a flat-term K-flat representative P, postcompose the desired augmentation square with the target reduction counit and the invertible exact-pullback factor. The defining representative equation of the strict reduction comparison rewrites one path. The chosen normalization of completedReductionTowerUnit rewrites both augmentation edges as localizations of their ordinary strict quotient-unit maps. Naturality of the exact tower-pullback localization factor and the ordinary comparison's defining augmentation equation identify the two paths. Cancel the invertible target counit. Fully faithful restriction to flat-term K-flat representatives extends this equality of natural transformations to all derived objects. Pullback preserves K-flatness for these representatives by the ringed-topos pullback theorem. This proves stratumReduction_augmentation for the actual chosen maps and every f, without imposing any stratum hypothesis on f.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); explicit quotient-normalization formula in def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum.

proof.text: stratumRestriction_limits supplies all-limit preservation for the actual module pullback, hence its canonical countable product comparisons are invertible. Apply the fully proved product-preserving-derived-limit-mate theorem to this functor. Its ordinary identity-component constant square is the inverse of d.constantPullbackIso; exact localization respects this inverse. Expanding the mate formula identifies its component with the specified stratumRlimComparison, so that actual map is invertible on every strict derived tower. Compose with derived limit of the normalized reduction-tower isomorphism for completion comparison invertibility. This preserves the prescribed comparison, arbitrary unbounded towers, and arbitrary non-Noetherian Y.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), especially Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); canonical exact-product comparison and augmentation clause of lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit.

proof.text: Prove the specified completion-unit equation directly by adjunction naturality and triangle identities, using the existing stratumReduction_augmentation declaration. Write F for derived module pullback, G for derived tower pullback, E for the constant/pullback isomorphism, and R for the target Rlim. Naturality of the target adjunction unit moves F(eta_K) past that unit; naturality of E.inv moves the source constant functor across F(eta_K). The source counit naturality and triangle identity reduce constant(eta_K) followed by the counit to the quotient augmentation. Apply the strict augmentation identity and cancel E.inv with E.hom. Functoriality of R gives exactly the target completion unit, with its specified source. Invertibility of the comparison follows by composing stratumRlimComparison_isIso with R of the tower isomorphism. Strict augmentation compatibility is proved by the preceding representative calculation; inverse-limit invertibility is proved in step 5.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), normalized kernel inclusion in the proof; proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), with unit compatibility supplied by the cited statements.

proof.text: Apply completedKoszulQuotientComparison separately on X and Y to the supplied representatives. It identifies each intrinsic completion unit followed by an isomorphism with the actual quotient completion unit. Thus invertibility of the source intrinsic unit implies invertibility of its quotient unit. Pull it back and compose with the isomorphism stratumCompletionComparison; the unit equation of the preceding step gives invertibility of the target quotient unit. Cancel the target Koszul/quotient comparison isomorphism to obtain invertibility of the specified target intrinsic unit. No new representative or generating list is substituted.

Preservation gives the forward implication for each composite of a stratum immersion with a chosen covering-member weakly-etale morphism. Conversely, choose a complex representative of each pulled-back object and use the hypothesis and the Koszul/quotient comparison to make each local quotient unit invertible. The completion comparison and its unit equation then make every pullback of the global quotient unit invertible. For joint detection, upgrade the supplied locally closed partition to the existing constructible Stratification using the Noetherian underlying space. The canonical module/abelian unit mate gives a natural isomorphism between the underlying identified-coefficient module pullback and abelian inverse image. Apply the existing abelian stratum-cover zero-detection theorem to the underlying cohomology sheaves in every degree. Exact pullback commutes with cohomology, so it jointly detects zero derived objects. Apply that to a distinguished cone of the global quotient unit, using triangulatedness of exact pullback, to conclude that the global unit is invertible. Cancel the global Koszul/quotient comparison to recover the specified intrinsic condition. Empty strata and covers, unbounded complexes, and non-Noetherian covering members require no additional hypotheses.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication, completeness devissage; stratum detection via Stacks proetale.tex Tags 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open) and 09AB (lemma-thickening).

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2) and Proposition 6.6.11 reverse implication. The ordinary strict comparison is normalized by its quotient augmentation and descended using computing counits. B4 proves finite quotient normalization by identifying each scalar normalization with the mate of inverse restriction composition, proving geometric pullback coherence for successive scalar restrictions, and applying a generic proved composition law for mates. The existing finite evaluation obligation remains. Strict augmentation, limit comparison, completion-unit and completeness proofs are retained. No statement, definition, chosen datum or unit route changes.

lean.statement: theorem stratum_completion_unit_restriction (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X] (S : FiniteLocallyClosedStratification X) (V : ∀ i : Fin S.n, Scheme.Cover.{w} proetalePrecoverage (S.domain i)) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = d.ideal) (K : d.derived X) (C : CochainComplex (reductionModules X (d.completedRing X)) ℤ) (eC : DerivedCategory.Q.obj C ≅ K) : IsDerivedCompleteIntrinsic X d r a ha K C eC ↔ ∀ (i : Fin S.n) (j : (V i).I₀), ∀ (D : CochainComplex (reductionModules ((V i).X j) (d.completedRing ((V i).X j))) ℤ) (eD : DerivedCategory.Q.obj D ≅ (d.pull ((V i).f j ≫ S.immersion i)).obj K), IsDerivedCompleteIntrinsic ((V i).X j) d r a ha ((d.pull ((V i).f j ≫ S.immersion i)).obj K) D eD
